claim: RAG fine-tunes both the DPR question encoder and the document encoder in its reported training procedure.
Their shared encoder-decoder and denoising properties establish that T5 historically influenced BART.
The FiD method requires T5 and excludes BART as a possible sequence-to-sequence model.
RAG uses a BART-large generator and fine-tunes that generator in the reported procedure.
RAG keeps its BART generator parameters fixed throughout the reported fine-tuning.
RAG initializes its retriever from DPR and keeps the document encoder fixed during its reported fine-tuning.
The reported DPR retriever shares one BERT encoder parameter set between questions and passages.
T5 describes BERT as the sole inspiration for its baseline denoising objective.
T5 describes its baseline denoising objective as inspired by BERT masked language modelling and word dropout.
T5 and BART can be compared as encoder-decoder approaches with denoising pre-training.
FiD reports DPR retrieval for Natural Questions and TriviaQA, and BM25 for SQuAD.
The comparison establishes that FiD loads a previously trained RAG system as a component.
The FiD paper compares its handling of retrieved passages with RAG and describes joint processing in the decoder.
FiD uses DPR for every dataset reported in the paper.
The reported DPR retriever uses two independent BERT encoders for questions and passages.
The reported FiD experiments initialize from T5; the method description also allows a model such as BART.
BART is initialized by loading a released BERT checkpoint.
The BART paper compares its bidirectional encoder with BERT within a broader sequence-to-sequence architecture.
